CycleTwin
Synthetic cycle forecasting for clinician decision support
Digital Twin Challenge 2026 · Kushagra Gupta · VIT
Synthetic engineering prototype · no clinical validation
Not for diagnosis, contraception or conception planning.

The forecasting question
02
Can a system flag a likely delayed or absent ovulation early in a 
cycle, while showing uncertainty and limits?
•
Target: synthetic anovulation or ovulation after cycle day 21
•
Forecast points: cycle days 10, 14 and 18
•
Decision-support framing; no diagnostic or reproductive-planning use

PMOS is a multi-system condition
03
Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS; PCOS/PCOD)
The project frames the problem across reproductive and metabolic signals. The 
synthetic build currently evaluates only a reproductive-axis proxy.
Terminology follows Teede et al., The Lancet, 2026. The simulated phenotype labels are not diagnostic criteria.

Why a digital-twin framing
04
Planned design
• Reproductive follicle and ovulation 
dynamics
•
Metabolic glucose dynamics
• Shared insulin-resistance latent with 
reverse cycle coupling
Current build
•
Stochastic synthetic cycle generator
• Fixed risk score and temperature 
coverline heuristic
• Simplified coupled twin shown in 
dashboard; not calibrated

Data fusion and sensor tiers
05
Tier 0
Period logs
›
Tier 1
+ resting HR*
›
Tier 2
+ nightly temp
›
Tier 3
+ CGM 
windows
›
Tier 4
+ EHR labs
Implemented evaluator: neutral period-only score; tier 1 uses resting-heart-rate offsets; tier 2 adds 
nightly temperature.
* Other wearable streams are generated but not fused. CGM display is synthetic only; E2 and EHR tiers are not evaluated.

Synthetic data and leakage control
06
•
1,200 synthetic patients × 6 cycles per generator seed
•
Three fresh seeds: 97, 101, 103
•
Patient-level split: 70% train, 15% validation, 15% held-out test
•
No personal exports, credentialed data or external health records
The generator carries latent traits and noisy observations; the evaluator separates patients across partitions.

Forecast model
07
Risk score
•
Tier 0: neutral baseline
•
Tier 1: resting-heart-rate offset
• Tier 2: temperature rise relative to an early-
cycle baseline
Ovulation-day estimate
•
Temperature coverline heuristic
•
Fallback: forecast day + 10
• Dashboard twin is separate and 
uncalibrated; no EKF
Conformal coverage is not reported. All settings are simulator assumptions.

Safety and abstention
08
Dashboard safety rules
•
Review for thyroid/prolactin flags
• Abstain for contraception and pregnancy-
related states
• Abstain for age and sensor completeness 
conditions
• Dashboard shows a synthetic risk-coverage 
diagnostic
Current status
G2 dashboard implements explicit 
abstention guards. Safety 
performance and conformal 
coverage are not evaluated.

Synthetic held-out results
09
Tier 2 · forecast day 14 · held-out patients
Seed 97: AUROC 0.637 · AUPRC 0.598 · Brier 0.306 · event rate 0.506
Seed 101: AUROC 0.638 · AUPRC 0.604 · Brier 0.316 · event rate 0.523
Seed 103: AUROC 0.663 · AUPRC 0.615 · Brier 0.309 · event rate 0.511
Patient-cluster bootstrap 95% intervals for AUROC and AUPRC are in results.json. Synthetic generator performance 
only.
No comparison with real-world published accuracy is made.

Illustrative counterfactuals
10
Planned scenario inputs
• Regular 7–8 hour sleep
• Daily 30-minute walk
• Lower-glycaemic-index Indian food swap
• Lower evening stress
• Illustrative 5% weight change
Current status
The dashboard shows hand-set risk 
ranges. No twin-based or generator 
counterfactuals are implemented. 
Effects are assumptions, not 
treatment advice.
Planned label: illustrative assumption, not a treatment recommendation.

Robustness and failure modes
11
•
Current robustness sweeps are not implemented
•
No wearable dropout, fever, travel or shift-work stress tests
•
No simulator-shift experiment
•
Known limitation: generator labels and signals share the same simplified assumptions
The synthetic benchmark cannot establish performance under real sensor noise or clinical variation.

Dashboard and Apple Health input
12
•
Streaming XML parser for a limited HealthKit export subset
•
Risk-ranked synthetic list, timeline, abstention banner and alert log
•
Synthetic CGM panel, marginal conformal range and illustrative what-if controls
•
CSV adapter supports date, temp, rhr, hrv, steps, period_start
The synthetic export is a schema-compatibility smoke test, n=1; it clinically validates nothing.

Related work
13
•
Goodale 2019 · Luo 2020 · Wang 2025: wearable signals, differing prediction targets
•
Awoniran 2026 preprint · vaginal temperature; Shamanna 2025 · single-patient twin case
•
Lin 2023 · cycle glucose; Teede 2023 guideline and 2026 PMOS name consensus
•
Gibbs & Candès 2021 · adaptive conformal; Collins 2024 · TRIPOD+AI
•
mcPHASES is a restricted-access roadmap source; no data are used
These works inform terminology, design and reporting. They do not validate this synthetic simulator.

Limits and next steps
14
•
Calibrate and connect the coupled twin to the E1 forecast
•
Evaluate abstention and marginal conformal coverage on untouched data
•
Add CGM/EHR prediction tiers, counterfactual simulation and robustness tests
•
Seek clinician co-design and real-data validation before any clinical use
